summary: ASHA opposes tying E-Rate decisions to educational outcomes, emphasizing the importance of maintaining access to communication tools and disability-related services for students. ASHA comments on the importance of E-Rate for supporting communication and technology services in schools and libraries. ASHA supports reasonable measures to prevent fraud, waste, and abuse in the E-Rate program, but urges the Commission to exclude AAC use, hearing-related accessibility tools, captioning, digital assessment, technology-enabled intervention activities, and telepractice from any screen time limit imposed as a condition of E-Rate funding.
